newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says border incident with Peru is over.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says border incident with Peru is over.

text.p: Ecuador said the return on Thursday of seven of its soldiers, who were arrested by Peru for crossing into a disputed border zone, had put an end to the incident with its Andean neighbour.
"The handover puts an end to this incident," Foreign Minister Jose Ayala told journalists.

Peru captured an Ecuadorean army patrol on Wednesday, charging that the seven soldiers were laying mines on its side of the border. The soldiers were handed back to Ecuador on Thursday morning, a Peruvian army captain told Reuters.

The incident inflamed tensions between the two countries, whose forces fought a month-long border war in 1995 over a disputed stretch of frontier jungle. Dozens of soldiers were killed and hundreds injured on both sides.

The head of Ecuador's armed forces, Gen. Paco Moncayo, on Wednesday rejected the Peruvian charge that his troops were laying mines in the border zone. But he admitted the patrol might have strayed into undisputed Peruvian territory.
The latest confrontation came as Ecuadorean and Peruvian officials were set to start a second round of talks in Brasilia to settle the decades-old border dispute.
Peru's acting Foreign Minister Jorge Gonzalez Izquierdo said he regretted the Ecuadorean incursion, but was confident the peace dialogue would stay on track.
Gen. Moncayo said the Ecuadorean patrol had been on a routine mission. He disputed the Peruvian charge that the troops were found with 600 anti-personnel mines.
"That's something you can't believe. How can seven men walk seven kilometres with 600 landmines?" he said.
Moncayo said Ecuadorean and Peruvian troops often cross over into each others territory along the jungle frontier.
Moncayo said that there was no fighting in the incident and that no one was hurt. He said the Ecuadorean authorities had ordered an investigation.
